name: aft.page
description: Deploy HTML or dist/ to a live HTTPS URL. No account. Drop, MCP, or CLI.
author: page.aft
readme:
# aft **Open source.** Vercel-like DX for frontends — deploy into **your** cloud (AWS or Cloudflare). Static / SPA today on both; Next.js SSR on AWS. ```bash aft deploy # default: AWS → CloudFront aft deploy --provider cloudflare # Cloudflare Pages aft deploy --env staging aft rollback dep_… --env production aft ui ``` License: **Apache-2.0** · Requires **Node 22+** ([nvm](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm): `nvm use` — see `.nvmrc`) ![aft detect + deploy --dry-run](./docs/assets/aft-hello-dry-run.svg)

## Providers | Provider | Status | What you get | | --- | --- | --- | | **AWS** | ✅ Supported | S3 + CloudFront; Next.js SSR via OpenNext + Lambda | | **Cloudflare** | ✅ Supported | Cloudflare Pages (static / SPA); custom domain optional | | **GCP / Azure** | 🔜 Coming soon | Same CLI shape, your account | Set once in `aft.json` (`"provider": "aws" | "cloudflare"`) or pass `--provider` per deploy. ## Why open source? - You connect **your** cloud account — the deploy engine should be auditable. - CLI auth is your existing cloud login (AWS CLI profile, or Cloudflare API token / wrangler OAuth) — no proprietary aft account required. - Local workset DB on your machine (`~/.aft/aft.sqlite`). Hosted “aft Cloud” + team auth come later. ## Mission: make agent-built apps real Agents make purpose-built personal and small-team software quickly. `aft` removes the AWS/Cloudflare ceremony between that output and a durable URL in your own account. It is the portable, customer-cloud path of the broader [aft.page Small Software mission](https://aft.page). ## Important use case: gated internal tools The best fit isn’t another marketing site — it’s the small app you build when an API is down, a CMS is too heavy, or ops needs a one-off UI **today**. **Today (deploy):** ship the frontend to your AWS or Cloudflare account (or `*.aft.page`), get a link, share it in chat. **Coming soon (auth):** put Google or Microsoft login in front of that link — company domain only, invite a teammate, revoke when you’re done. No hardcoded email lists, no client-side “admin” checks that APIs ignore. ```text pain → small app → aft deploy → live URL ↓ (soon) Google / Microsoft gate invite · revoke · domain allow ``` Classic failure mode without that layer: Google login on the UI, allowlist in the bundle, and `/api/*` routes with no session check — auth looks real, data is still open. aft’s job is deploy **and** a real gate so internal tools don’t reinvent that wrong. ## Hello World (first deploy) The shortest path from zero → a planned deploy. **No cloud credentials** until the last step. ```bash # 1. Install aft from this repo git clone https://github.com/vaibhavmule/aft.git cd aft && nvm use && npm install && npm run build && npm link # 2. Try the bundled static example (no cloud account) cd examples/hello aft detect aft deploy --dry-run # Or from the repo root: npm run demo ``` **AWS** (needs CloudFront create access): ```bash cd examples/hello aws sts get-caller-identity --profile aft # any profile with S3 + CloudFront aft deploy --profile aft aft ui ``` **Cloudflare** (static): ```bash cd examples/hello export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=… # or: npx wrangler login export CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=… aft deploy --provider cloudflare # optional: --domain example.com ``` On AWS you get: | URL | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `https://{cf}/` | Production (current deploy) | | `https://{cf}/d/{depId}/` | Immutable URL for that deploy | | `aft ui` | Local workset — projects, history, destroy | Teardown anytime: `aft destroy --yes` (AWS path). ## Install (from source) ```bash git clone https://github.com/vaibhavmule/aft.git cd aft nvm use # Node 22+ npm install npm run build npm link # puts `aft` on your PATH ``` npm publish / package name TBD (`aft` is taken on npm). ## Architecture ```text Your laptop Your cloud ─────────── ────────── aft CLI ──creds──► AWS: S3 + CloudFront (+ Lambda SSR) aft.json Cloudflare: Pages project (+ optional domain) .aft/state.json ~/.aft/aft.sqlite aft ui (localhost:8787) ``` **Three persistence layers** (do not conflate them): | Layer | Where | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `aft.json` | Project root (often committed) | Name, provider, region, dir, spa, public env defaults | | `.aft/state.json` | Project root (gitignored) | Live resource IDs + owning account id | | `~/.aft/aft.sqlite` | Machine-local | Cross-project history for `aft status` / `aft ui` | **AWS static / SPA:** detect → optional build → upload to `deploys/{depId}/` → ensure CloudFront + OAC → point env at that deploy → invalidate → record workset. **Cloudflare static / SPA:** detect → optional build → ensure Pages project → upload directory → optional custom domain. **AWS URLs:** production = distribution root (`OriginPath`); named envs = `/e/{env}/`; every deploy keeps `/d/{depId}/` forever until you prune. **Safety (AWS):** destroy/rollback refuse the wrong account; partial deploys checkpoint state so `aft destroy` can finish cleanup; static↔SSR switch requires destroy first. ## Framework support | Framework | Today | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Static HTML | ✅ | Just `index.html` — see `examples/hello` | | React (Vite) | ✅ | Auto build → `dist/` — see `examples/vite-spa` | | React (CRA / Rsbuild) | ✅ | → `build/` | | Vue / Vite | ✅ | → `dist/` | | Next.js static export | ✅ | `output: 'export'` → `out/` | | Next.js SSR | ✅ AWS | OpenNext → Lambda + CloudFront; Cloudflare provider is static-only for now | | APIs / servers | 🔜 | Later | ## Auth (CLI credentials) No aft account. Use whatever the provider already knows: ```bash # AWS aws sts get-caller-identity aft deploy aft deploy --profile work # Cloudflare export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=… export CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=… aft deploy --provider cloudflare ``` ## Quick start (your app) ```bash cd my-app aft init aft deploy --dry-run # plan only — no cloud calls aft deploy # AWS production → CloudFront + /d/{depId}/ aft deploy --provider cloudflare # or Cloudflare Pages aft deploy --env staging # AWS named env aft rollback # list versioned deploys (AWS) aft rollback dep_… --env production aft status aft ui # http://127.0.0.1:8787 ``` ### Unique URLs, environments, rollback (static / SPA) Each deploy uploads to an immutable S3 prefix and stays reachable at: `https://{cloudfront}/d/{depId}/` Named environments point at a current deploy (no rebuild on rollback): | Environment | URL | | --- | --- | | `production` (default) | `https://{cloudfront}/` | | `staging`, `dev`, … | `https://{cloudfront}/e/{env}/` | ```bash aft deploy --env staging aft rollback dep_a1b2c3 --env staging ``` Or **aft ui** → deploy history → **Preview** / **Make live**. Next.js SSR: production URL only for now (Lambda versioning later). ### Environment variables aft loads env the same way Vercel-ish builds do — **no Secrets Manager for v1**. | Source | Typical use | | --- | --- | | `.env` | Shared non-secrets (can commit) | | `.env.local` | Secrets (gitignored) | | `.env.production` / `.env.production.local` | Production overrides | | `aft.json` → `"env": { … }` | Public defaults | | Shell / CI `process.env` | Highest precedence | - **Static / SPA:** vars are injected into the build process (`VITE_*`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, etc.). - **Next.js SSR:** same for OpenNext build, plus user vars on the **server Lambda**. - Values are never logged. ### Destroy ```bash aft destroy # live AWS inventory (BEFORE) — nothing deleted yet aft destroy --yes # delete PRESENT resources, then re-check (AFTER must be empty) ``` Destroy only archives the local workset row when the **after** probe finds nothing left in AWS (S3, CloudFront, OACs, functions, SSR stack). If something remains, state is kept so you can retry. Or open **aft ui** → project → **Destroy**: live PRESENT list → type project name → destroy + verify. ## What it creates in your account **AWS — static / SPA** - Private **S3** bucket (`aft--`) - **CloudFront** distribution + Origin Access Control - SPA fallback (403/404 → `/index.html`) - Per-project state in `.aft/state.json` (gitignored) **AWS — Next.js SSR (OpenNext)** - Same S3 bucket for assets + ISR cache - **Lambda** (server, image, revalidate) with IAM Function URLs - **DynamoDB** + **SQS** for ISR - **CloudFront** routing static → S3, rest → Lambda **Cloudflare — static / SPA** - **Cloudflare Pages** project - Optional custom domain via `--domain` - Per-project state in `.aft/state.json` (gitignored) ## Examples | Path | Kind | | --- | --- | | [`examples/hello`](./examples/hello) | Static HTML — **start here** | | [`examples/vite-spa`](./examples/vite-spa) | React + Vite SPA | | [`examples/next-ssr`](./examples/next-ssr) | Next.js SSR (OpenNext) | ## Local workset Every successful deploy writes to **`~/.aft/aft.sqlite`**: - `proj_…` project id (stable per folder path) - `dep_…` deployment id + Deployment Summary - estimated monthly cost (rough, not your AWS bill) `aft ui` lists projects and deploy history. Localhost only. ## Roadmap | Now (OSS CLI) | Next | Later | | --- | --- | --- | | AWS + Cloudflare providers | Custom domains (ACM + DNS) | GCP / Azure providers | | Static / SPA + AWS `/d/` URLs | Official GitHub Action | aft Cloud (hosted workset) | | Named envs `--env` + rollback | SSR env / rollback parity | Pretty URLs (`*.aft.dev`) | | Next.js SSR on AWS (OpenNext) | Cloudflare SSR / Workers | Opt-in telemetry (default off) | | Local `aft ui` + destroy verify | **App auth** (Google / Microsoft, domain gate) | Invite + revoke for internal tools | | Mock tests + CI (Node 22/24) | npm publish (scoped name) | | CloudFront account verification is an AWS Support step — once unlocked, `aft deploy --profile aft` on `examples/hello` is the smoke test. ## Demo (no AWS) ```bash npm run demo # detect + dry-run on examples/hello ``` Seed a fake workset and open the UI (for screenshots / PH gallery): ```bash AFT_HOME=/tmp/aft-demo-ui node --import tsx scripts/seed-demo-workset.ts AFT_HOME=/tmp/aft-demo-ui npm run aft -- ui --port 8787 --no-open # open http://127.0.0.1:8787 ``` Recording notes: [docs/demo.md](./docs/demo.md) · launch checklist: [LAUNCH.md](./LAUNCH.md). ## Troubleshooting ### CloudFront: “account must be verified” New AWS accounts often cannot create CloudFront until Support verifies them. aft checks this **before** creating storage. 1. Open [AWS Support](https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/home#/) 2. Case type **Account** → category **Account Verification** 3. Subject / description: `Account Verification before I can add new CloudFront resources, currently it is blocked to create` 4. When the case is resolved, run `aft deploy` again. ### Node version aft needs **Node 22+** (`node:sqlite`). With nvm: ```bash nvm install # reads .nvmrc nvm use node -v # should be v22+ or v24+ ``` ### AWS profile ```bash aws sts get-caller-identity --profile my-profile aft deploy --profile my-profile ``` ## Tests & CI ```bash npm test # no AWS credentials required — mocks cover destroy/verify/promote npm run test:coverage # c8 text + lcov (see coverage/) npm run demo # Hello World dry-run (also no AWS) ``` GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs typecheck + tests on **Node 22 and 24**. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for how mock AWS clients and `AFT_HOME` work. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License Apache-2.0 — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).
